messages:
marco: Hey — I twisted my knee last week and my PCP recommended PT. Quick Qs: does our medical plan require prior auth for PT? Any session limits/year? How do I find an in-network PT near me (SF)? If I go out-of-network, what's the reimbursement process and expected timeline?

sarah_benefits: Sorry to hear that, hope you're okay. For Redwood's standard PPO plan: most PT services do need a prior auth if they're >8 sessions or if they’re for post-op rehab. For acute injuries the plan often approves an initial block.

sarah_benefits: Session limits: baseline is 8 eval/tx visits without prior auth. Beyond that, submit a PA with the PT eval and treatment plan — appeals can add more.

lina-peopleops: To find in-network: log into Benefits Portal -> Coverage -> Find a Provider, filter "Physical Therapy" + city/zip. Link is https://benefits.redwood.com/providers (or DM me and I can pull a list) :point_right:

mike_j: FYI I used PT in SoMa last year — provider "MotionWorks PT" was in-network and billed straight to the plan, no OOP except copay. Very quick.

julie_claims: OON reimbursement steps if you pay upfront: 1) get itemized receipt with provider NPI and CPT codes, 2) fill OON claim form (attached in portal), 3) send to claims@insurer-example.com. Typical turnaround 7–14 business days after received docs.

julie_claims: Common PT CPT codes to include:
```
97110 - Therapeutic exercises
97112 - Neuromuscular reeducation
97140 - Manual therapy techniques
```
julie_claims: If you submit a PA, include the PT evaluation, recommended frequency/duration, and ICD-10 dx code from your PCP — that speeds approval.

marco: Thanks all — two small follow-ups: 1) Is there an expedited route for acute injury requests? 2) Can People Ops submit the PA on my behalf or does the PT clinic typically do it?

lina-peopleops: We can help shepherd it. If you authorize us we can open a case with the insurer and attach docs, but the PT clinic often submits the clinical PA since they have the eval and tx plan. If you want us to coordinate, DM me the provider name and a signed release phrase (e.g., "I authorize Redwood People Ops to submit benefits info on my behalf") and I'll escalate.

sarah_benefits: Expedited requests: insurer offers a 48–72hr turnaround for urgent acute cases — mark as "expedited/urgent" and include notes about limited mobility or risk of loss of function. Add "expedite" in the subject when filing.

julie_claims: Also note preauthorization doesn't guarantee full coverage for OON providers — you'll want an in-network referral if possible to minimize OOP.

marco: Great — DMing provider name now. One last thing: my digital ID card only shows the primary member; how do I get the dependent/secondary insurance info onto the card? Needed for intake at the PT front desk.

lina-peopleops: If the dependent is enrolled, the digital card should show both covered members. If it's missing, send a screenshot of your card + dependent name to benefits@redwood.com and we'll request an updated card PDF from insurer. Meanwhile, print the portal member summary (shows coverage and group/policy numbers) — front desks accept that 99% of the time.

hr-bot: Helpful links: Benefits Portal provider search: https://benefits.redwood.com/providers | OON claim form: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/oon-claim.pdf | PA checklist: https://benefits.redwood.com/pa-checklist.pdf :white_check_mark:

marco: Awesome, thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help :pray:
